svg.text: The whole process: one pilot seen from the other side
The infinite H, step by step. The Θ-pilot of † is the q-pilot of ‡ as far as the link can tell. Rebuilt inside one ring structure from the shared core, it becomes a region with fuzzy edges,
and comparing log-volumes gives the inequality of Cor 3.12.
up and down the column of †
The procession: tensor packets of log-shells
Column j is the container S±_(j+1) = {0, …, j}: j + 1
copies of the mono-analytic log-shell, rebuilt from the
core (grid). The top cell carries the theta value q̲^(j²)
(dots). The label of each cell is known only up to (j+1)!
leading-term heuristic of the toolkit: hull enlargement 47.1465,
Σ_j [(j+1)·log d^K − (j²/2l)·log q] = 198.1713, divided by l* = 6
The observer stays inside the ring structure of one theater the whole
time. The q-pilot is measured there directly (dots). The Θ-pilot is rebuilt
there from the shared core, so it is known only as a region (broken lines):
its log-volume is an upper bound.
Whether step 6 is a valid comparison is the disputed point of the theory ([IUTchIII] Cor
3.12). The plate draws what the toolkit computes, not a verdict.
outline only: a type, not a set
Every chip names a data type of the toolkit (species ids of `iut species`, C structs of src/iut.h). All numbers are read from `iut walk`.
